A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we nearly match the previous best lower bounds for $k$medians and $k$-mean, and give the first upper bounds for $k\geq 3$ for these two problems that are independent of $n$.

we give nearly tight bounds on the approximation ratios of explainable $k$-clusterings for the $k \geq 2$-medians, $k \ge 2$-means, and $\ell_p$ for any constant $p \ge 1$, and we give an oblivious algorithm that runs in nearly linear time.
we nearly-tightened the upper bounds for the $k=1$ case, and nearly-tightened both the upper and lower bounds for the general case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cost of explainability is not too high for the $k \ll d$ case that is of most interest.
the $k$ clusters in an optimal clustering need not be spread out across all the dimensions of the data, as long as they are well-separated in a few dimensions.
the $O(k)$ factor loss in explainability is unavoidable in the worst case, but for a large range of data sets, one can expect to lose a much smaller factor of $O(1)$.
